'''Baradium''' was a highly volatile element used in [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]] and was used to create some of the most powerful explosive weapons in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Depleted baradium could be used as [[Slug/Legends|slugs]].<ref name="TORCDenova">{{TORcite|type=codex|Denova}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
===Overview===
Although baradium was described as a "synthetic element,"<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> it may have existed in some form in naturally occurring lodes, as quantities of it were discovered on [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] and [[Anobis]] after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]];<ref name="LFT">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref> these may have been industrial by-products, however. During the [[Republic Dark Age]], the surface of [[Chelloa]] contained vast deposits of baradium which could be tapped by exploding the ground.<ref name="KnightErrant1">[[Knight Errant 1|''Knight Errant'' 1]]</ref>

The destructive force was described as a fusion reaction,<ref name="TDDB">{{DB|technology|thermaldetonator|thermal detonator}}</ref> and the majority of the energy produced was released as heat. A second component of a baradium explosion was a particle field, which formed the outer surface of the blast sphere, and which was sustained by the energy of the explosion inside: this had the useful effect of containing the destructive effect within a relatively precise perimeter. But although baradium was a very potent explosive, it was extremely unstable: accidental detonation could be triggered by careless use, and would have a devastating effect.<ref name="ISB" /> These factors placed important limits on the employment of baradium munitions. Baradium also caused poisoning after detonation.<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

===Thermal detonators===
{{Main|Thermal detonator/Legends}}
[[File:RotJ_Leia_holding_Thermal_Detonator.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Thermal detonators (pictured) made use of baradium]]
Probably the best-known and most widespread form of baradium charge was a type known as a thermal detonator. The standard thermal detonators used by the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] had a five-meter blast radius, and could penetrate up to two meters of [[Permacite/Legends|permacite]], but they were designed to be placed manually against hardened targets, rather than lobbed as grenades or mortar rounds.<ref name="ISB" /> They were issued to [[Imperial Combat Engineer]]s<ref name="ISB" /> and to [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="TDDB" />

Other thermal detonators were used by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]; these had a twenty-meter radius.<ref name="TDDB" /> These were used as suicide weapons by terrorists.<ref name="CoPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> The ostentatious destructive potential of larger thermal detonators is perhaps best illustrated by the fact that a single [[Class-A thermal detonator/Legends|Class-A thermal detonator]], detonating in the basement, brought down [[Xizor's Palace]], one of the largest buildings on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="SotE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

Baradium was the active ingredient of [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[vape charge]]s, which were used by the [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force]] for demolition purposes.<ref name="Dark Nest III: The Swarm War>''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref>

===Baradium missiles===
Much more powerful even than this were [[baradium missile]]s, which were capable of destroying [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] in a single blast. One of these was acquired by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and supplied to the [[Myrkr strike team]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. Carrying a charge of one [[Metric ton/Legends|metric ton]] of baradium, the blast-radius of a detonation in space was a full [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]] wide. To help ensure that it reached its target, it had [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], and sufficient maneuverability to evade the defenses of enemy warships, both controlled by a [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brain]] pilot.<ref name="SbS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

Several racks of baradium missiles were later found in the [[Missile Hold]] aboard the [[Anakin Solo (starship)|Star Destroyer ''Anakin Solo'']]. These had a trigger mechanism using a [[Deuterium/Legends|deuterium]]-based [[Proton grenade/Legends|proton charge]], which on its own was capable of producing a blast comparable to some thermal detonators.<ref name="LFT" />

In [[44 ABY]], baradium missiles were used during the [[Battle over Exodo II]] by the forces of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Drikl Lecersen]] to destroy the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Gilad Pellaeon (starship)|''Gilad Pellaeon'']] and the moon [[Boreleo]].

===Baradium fission device===
Baradium was also used in the construction of [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] that were capable of destroying an entire planet. [[Baradium fission device]]s existed during both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial eras]]. However, these weapons were banned sometime during the early Imperial era by the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Senate]] via legislation strongly supported by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] did manage to obtain one baradium fission device and planned to use the device to destroy the [[Bilbringi Shipyards|Imperial Shipyards]] orbiting the planet [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]]. This mission ended in failure when the [[Quip Fargil|pilot]] charged to deliver the weapon ditched the device because he was unwilling to sacrifice the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].

===Baradium bomb===
During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], [[Imperial Agent]] [[Cipher Nine]] had to defuse a [[Baradium bomb/Legends|baradium bomb]] that the [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]] had intended to use to destroy the [[Voss (species)|Voss]] capital city of [[Voss-Ka]]. The Gormak built the device from scavenged hardware and copied the design from existing [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] baradium bombs. Ultimately Cipher Nine was successful in preventing the destruction of Voss-Ka.

===Other baradium weapons===
In small quantities, baradium could be used with some precision: [[thermal detonator tape]] was used to breach [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]], for example.<ref name="RCTZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref>

A more specialized form of baradium weapon was the [[Seismic charge/Legends|seismic charge]], in which the baradium was combined with [[collapsium]]. Rather than a spherical blast radius, the destructive power of a seismic charge was constrained into a narrow plane, producing a violent shearing effect through anything in the path of the blast.<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref><ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

In an attempt to counteract the instability of baradium-based thermal detonators, the Alliance to Restore the Republic developed the [[thermal well]], which combined baradium with [[ytterbium]], to produce a much more stable explosive compound. This burned at several thousand degrees Celsius and was capable of melting most objects within its blast radius.<ref name="RoE">''[[Rules of Engagement: The Rebel SpecForce Handbook]]''</ref>

While baradium was normally used as an explosive, depleted baradium was used to make dense, small-caliber bullets. The [[YVH 1|YVH series]] could carry a depleted-baradium pellet launcher capable of shredding [[yorik coral]].<ref name="SbS" />

==History==
Baradium's destructive power meant that thermal detonators and more powerful models remained illegal under the Galactic Empire,<ref name="TDDB" /> while unauthorized possession of a thermal detonator was punishable by death.<ref name="ISB" /> But while a small baradium charge was issued as standard to stormtroopers, the cost of production and the problems involved in handling the material also meant that its use was limited, even within the massive military-industrial complex of the Imperial forces.<ref name="ISB" />

These limits did not completely prohibit the use of baradium weapons, however. Even under the Old Republic, thermal detonators were popular with bounty hunters and other fringe elements.<ref name="TDDB" /> During the Republic Dark Age, baradium was widely sought by [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] like [[Daiman]] and [[Odion]] for their war effort against the Republic and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. In [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]], a Jedi team under [[Vannar Treece]] raided [[Chelloa]] to disrupt Daiman's baradium supply line. During the [[Operation Influx|fighting]], Odion's forces deployed a massive [[kinetic corruptor]], which harnessed the baradium by exploding a chunk of the landscape and killing many of the combatants.<ref name="KnightErrant1" />

They were used by elite Imperial soldiers such as [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="TDDB" /> [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] was known as the primary manufacturer,<ref name="ISB" /> but a few other companies were authorized to produce detonators by the Empire, including [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]] subsidiary [[Tarascii Explosives/Legends|Tarascii Explosives]].<ref name="RoE" /> Large thermal detonators continued to be illegal under the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], although that did not stop [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] from keeping a few in his private arsenal aboard the ''Millennium Falcon''.<ref name="CoPL" />

The [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] saw the one recorded use of a baradium missile, by the [[Myrkr strike team]]. The primary plan of the strike team's mission was built around this weapon, which was to be used to destroy the [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] facility creating the [[voxyn]] at [[Myrkr/Legends|Myrkr]]. In the event, it was fired instead against a [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]], completely obliterating it even though it exploded half a kilometer from the warship's hull.<ref name="SbS" />

There is little further evidence for baradium missiles being regularly used in combat, however. The cache aboard the [[Anakin Solo (starship)|Star Destroyer ''Anakin Solo'']] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] may have been an anomaly, reflecting that ship's unusual role as [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]] of the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]]. During the [[Battle of Kashyyyk (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Kashyyyk]], for example, [[Darth Caedus]] carried out the [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] exclusively with the Star Destroyer's long range [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]].<ref name="LFI">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref>

After the war, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] attempted to reassert tight state control of baradium supplies, as a large-scale [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] operation it was considered a serious issue in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]].<ref name="TJK" /> Shortly before [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], however, large deposits of baradium were discovered on [[Duro/Legends|Duro]], and these would prove to be the ultimate catalyst for the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], when [[Thrackan Sal-Solo]] and his faction began secret military preparations to secure the supply for [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].<ref name="LFT" /> There was also several baradium missiles on hand for the New Jedi Order during the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Lost Tribe of Sith emergence)|Liberation of Coruscant]], however they were not used.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>
